pairs.question: quare vultus tuus tristis cum te aegrotum non videam non est hoc frustra sed malum nescio quid in corde tuo est?
pairs.answer: rex in aeternum vive quare non maereat vultus meus quia civitas domus sepulchrorum patris mei deserta est et portae eius conbustae sunt igni
pairs.derivation: The king's question in v.2 (introduced by the dropped speech tag 'dixitque mihi rex') asks why Nehemiah's face is sad; the trailing narration 'et timui valde ac nimis' is dropped as meta-narration. Nehemiah's reply in v.3 (speech tag 'et dixi regi' dropped) directly answers WHY his face is sad. The whole reply is the answer; it ends at the full stop closing v.3. Terminal punctuation normalized to '?' on the question.

pairs.question: pro qua re postulas?
pairs.answer: si videtur regi bonum et si placet servus tuus ante faciem tuam ut mittas me in Iudaeam ad civitatem sepulchri patris mei et aedificabo eam
pairs.derivation: The king's question 'pro qua re postulas' (v.4, speech tag 'et ait mihi rex' dropped). The reply's narrated preamble 'et oravi Deum caeli' (v.4) does not answer and is skipped; the answer advances to the operative answering content in v.5 (speech tag 'et dixi ad regem' dropped), which states the request. Capitalization of first word and terminal '?' normalized.

pairs.question: quae est haec res quam facitis numquid contra regem vos rebellatis?
pairs.answer: Deus caeli ipse nos iuvat et nos servi eius sumus surgamus et aedificemus vobis autem non est pars et iustitia et memoria in Hierusalem
pairs.derivation: Sanaballat and the others ask (v.19, after dropped framing 'subsannaverunt nos et despexerunt dixeruntque') what this thing is and whether they are rebelling against the king. Nehemiah's reply (v.20, framing 'et reddidi eis sermonem dixique ad eos' dropped) answers the accusation: God helps us, we are his servants, we will build, you have no share. The whole reply is the answer. Terminal '?' normalized.
